summary: The author asked what standard ETL suites do that the bare-bones setup cannot, gave his own experience of them in four points, and asked for the categories of functionality he should not miss.
verbatim:
Now I have a number of follow up questions.

* What is it that ETL tools do exactly that this "bare-bones" / "AI assisted" set up wouldn't be able to do, or would be noticeably more cumbersome?
* If I do it in the "bare-bones" manner, i.e. with md text files, generative principles, generating simple deterministic (SQL) engines etc, I can have it read and edited by LLMs quite simply.
* In my experience the standard ETL suites (like PowerCenter, SSIS, Azure Databricks) are able to do the bread and butter standard things, but they all have their own difficulties dealing with edge cases, which then require special interventions, voiding the advantage of having everything in one tool, or requiring 'weird' implementations and work arounds within the tool. In my opinion we often run into the limits of what is possible pretty quickly.
* Maybe sometimes the administration / management console of standard ETL tools is better, like authorizations, or integration with AD, or building DTAP streets and promoting strategies.
* I also don't find them helpful in keeping "overzicht" (for lack of a proper english translation. They become messy to look at pretty quickly, so they are not helpful in quickly comprehensing what is happening.

Maybe I am missing something, so please also give me the relevant categories of functionality that these ETL tools provide, and that I should not miss in this setup.

summary: Answered with thirteen capabilities the suites provide, where nsdn stands on each, a reply to each of his four points, and the advice to answer capabilities 1, 2, 5 and 6 with small parts or platform features.
notes: The tool side was from general knowledge, not checked. The answer said a DuckDB file has no users or roles; S12-037 found that to hold for a file used in process and found three serving options beside it. Logged from the conversation of 2026-11-14 on a different model from S12-001 to S12-027.

summary: The author asked for the findings to be stored and a separate research programme set up, tentatively an equivalence investigation, with Databricks' open-source parts as inspiration kept apart from the questions.
verbatim: Yes, please store these findings somewhere. They are real gaps that need to be addressed. They also comprise a kind of research project, i.e. we need to address these issues. Please set up this separate research program. Not sure what to call it, these are kind of non-functional requirements, but also functional requirements. Maybe this is an equivalence investigation, how to get this light-weight, bare bones, AI assisted programma on the same level as "enterprise grade" environments. What I also find interesting is that Databricks, which is becoming a kind of industry standard, is made up of several open source projects. Maybe we could also draw some inspiration from that. These are separate from the research questions, because in a way they are already answers. Interested to hear your thoughts.

The author ruled on the programme: a name conditional on the model's agreement, the subfolder, the order, a three-step method in place of the proposed outcomes, and five principles for bridging a gap.
verbatim: Yes, let's call it "Imperative ETL capability equivalence investigation" if you agree. Otherwise I'll go with your suggestion. Subfolder in 30_research seems appropriate. I agree on the order. With regards to the proposed outcomes, I think we mainly want to identify gaps, then identify requirements given a client's environment, size etc. and then judge if and how we should bridge the gap. From what I've seen, I don't think that any of the gaps are real showstoppers. Most of it should be doable, using some Apache licensed products. I think that given some thorough requirements analysis, a solid architecture, separation of concerns and generation guidelines an LLM is perfectly capable to design, build and implement most functionalities. This is what the project is about. Stay away from proprietary products, keep it all machine-readable (FAIR acronym), have the agentic layer manage, build and supervise the deterministic layer, use the human adjudication economy properly.
